description:
Found while writing examples/codecs.exs (defk-9p6.19): `alloc(u8, n)` zero-fills the buffer with one memset (defk_own in priv/defk_runtime.h), so an 85 MB allocation holds the scheduler for ~5 ms before the kernel's first loop runs; the tick gap during a 64 MB base64 encode was 4.6-6.6 ms, against the 2.3 ms a yielding loop keeps. Elixir mode defines alloc as a zeroed binary, so the zeroing must stay semantically; it does not have to be one memset.

Options: (a) zero in strips of a few MB with a safepoint between them (a loop in the generated C around the memset, charged to the budget like any loop; the frame must spill the partially-zeroed state: the alloc's slot index and the offset); (b) allocate without zeroing when the compiler can prove every element is written before any read (common: `for i <- ...: out[i] = ...` over the full range), keeping the memset otherwise; (c) both. Measure (b)'s win on scale/image_resize/codecs (memset is a full extra pass over the output).

Done when: an 85 MB alloc shows a worst tick gap in line with a yielding loop (bench/tick_gap.exs style test), and either (b) is implemented with a test on the generated C or recorded as a follow-up with numbers.

comments.text:
Implemented (c), on branch defk-ktw/alloc-zero-safepoints. All numbers were taken UNDER LOAD (3 other agents, load average 4-5). Each is the best of 2-3 script runs, each run the min of 60 reps (15 for the large cases).

Tick gap (bench/tick_gap.exs, 1 scheduler, 1 ms ticker, worst gap per run; idle ~2.1 ms, yielding kernel 2.25-2.5 ms):
- one 85 MB alloc, first run (cold pages): main 3.88 ms (3.88, 4.04 in other runs); branch 2.00-2.55 ms
- 20 x 85 MB alloc (one call each, warm, 6.9 ms in total): main 6.70-6.92 ms; branch 1.94-2.28 ms, 25 yields/run
- runtime of the 20-alloc run: 6.7-6.85 ms on main, 7.0 ms on the branch (it includes the ticker's turns)

Strip size: with 64 KiB strips a warm 85 MB alloc was ~30% slower than one memset (461 vs 350 us). With 1 MiB strips there was no measurable difference (316-342 vs 310-336 us), so DEFK_ZERO_STRIP is 1 MiB.

(b) throughput, main -> branch, under load:
- scale 1M f64: 170 -> 131 us (-23%)
- scale 10M f64: 1729 -> 1454 us (-16%)
- encode16 1 MB: 338 -> 297 us (-12%)
- encode64 1 MB and 256 KB: 222/57 vs 223/57 us, no change. The loop plus the tail writes is not a form (b) proves, so it is zeroed in strips.
- encode64 64 MB: 15.9-16.1 ms on both
- resize_bilinear 1080p -> 480x270: within noise (1324-1406 us on the branch vs 1349-1377 on main). The out buffer has a 2-D index (not proven, zeroed in strips); xo and xf are unzeroed.
An upper bound for (b), from skipping every memset (unsound): scale -15-25%, encode16/encode64 1 MB -8-12%, 64 MB -2-6%, resize noise.

title: A large alloc/2 zero-fills without a safepoint: 85 MB costs a 5 ms scheduler gap
